uncited: **Precompute Element Signatures:** For each element, compute the sign of the dot product between the element centroid $\mathbf{c}$ and each normal vector $\mathbf{n}_i$ defining its faces.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot M \cdot F)$, where $N$ is the number of pixels, $M$ is the number of visible elements, and $F$ is the number of faces per element.
This is potentially expensive for high-resolution images and complex meshes.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(M \cdot F)$ to store element signatures, plus $O(N)$ for the image buffer.
- **Strengths:** Decouples pixelization from mesh data structures; handles variable-resolution meshes; no vertex winding order required.
- **Limitations:** Limited to convex elements; nearest-neighbor interpolation may result in aliasing; performance degrades with high pixel counts and many elements.
- **When to use:** When working with unstructured meshes where vertex ordering is inconsistent or unknown, and when decoupling mesh data from rendering is required.
- **When not to use:** For non-convex meshes; when high-quality interpolation is required; for very large meshes with high-resolution images due to performance constraints.
